answers.answer: Top to bottom, the deck has 1 Conflict I card, 5 Conflict II cards, and 4 Conflict III cards. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Top to bottom: 1x Conflict I, 5x Conflict II, 4x Conflict III.” “Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and a third Agent (the Swordmaster) next to the board. Of 12 troops, 3 start in that player's nearest garrison and 9 in supply. Each starts with 1 water and one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Influence tracks. Starting VP is 0 in a three-player game and 1 in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Each player places 2 Agents on their Leader” and sets “their third Agent (their Swordmaster)” next to the board; 3 troops go in the nearest garrison and “the rest” of the 12 troops go in supply; each places one cube on the bottom of all four tracks; “Each player takes 1 water”; score marker is on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. Agent turns are optional, so you may Reveal while Agents remain. Once you have taken your Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase; you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue cards may be played only during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns, so you cannot play one later in the phase after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left.” “Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.” Plot Intrigue cards may be played “during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.”

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send one Agent to an unoccupied space. One card cannot send multiple Agents; a card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn. You must pay the space costs and meet its requirements before resolving any space or card effects; if unable to pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “play one card from your hand face up,” choose “only one Agent icon,” and send “one Agent” to an unoccupied space. “You can't send an Agent to a board space that already has an Agent on it.” “You must pay any costs and meet any requirements ... Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects.”

answers.answer: No. Entry costs must be paid immediately before resolving the space or played card effects, so the card's later spice gain cannot pay Conspire's 4-spice entry cost when you have only 3 spice. After legally entering, you may resolve the board-space effect, the card's Agent box, and the one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the played card”; “Gain the effects of the board space, the card's Agent box, and the one-space Influence advancement ... in any order, after paying the entry cost.” Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You can deploy at most 5 troops: all 3 recruited this turn, plus up to 2 from your garrison. Any recruited troops not deployed go to your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its four recruits go to your garrison and cannot normally be deployed there.
answers.evidence: At a Combat space, deploy “any or all troops you recruited this turn ... plus up to two more troops from your garrison.” “Recruited troops you don't deploy go to your garrison as usual.” Rally Troops recruits four troops and is “not a Combat space, so they go to your garrison.”

answers.answer: The Reveal turn steps are: (1) reveal all remaining hand cards; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of those revealed cards, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Cards played on Agent turns do not have their Reveal boxes resolved. During Clean Up, put all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn lists “1. Reveal Cards,” “2. Resolve Reveal Effects,” “3. Set Strength,” and “4. Clean Up.” Resolve the Reveal boxes “of the cards you just revealed (not of cards played during Agent turns earlier this round).” Clean Up puts “all the cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) into your discard pile.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may acquire the replacement card because the Imperium Row is refilled immediately and you may acquire its replacement if you can afford it. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split Persuasion from one source across cards. Unused Persuasion is lost and cannot be saved. Acquired cards go to your discard pile and cannot be used right away. An Acquire box effect happens once when you acquire the card.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: the Imperium Row “must always have five cards: refill it immediately ... so after acquiring a card you may also acquire its replacement.” Persuasion from sources may be pooled or split; “Persuasion can never be saved.” Acquired cards go to your discard pile; “you don't use them right away.” Acquire box effect occurs “at the moment you acquire the card.”

answers.answer: Three troops are worth 6 strength and four revealed swords add 4, for 10 total. If your last troop in the Conflict is removed, your strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. For strength over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop is worth 2 strength and each revealed sword is worth 1. “If your last troop is ever removed, your strength becomes 0 and can't be increased by any means, including swords.” If over 20, “flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.”

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing earlier does not prevent playing later. Combat resolves once all players involved pass consecutively. Cards that trigger “when you win a Conflict” are played after you have won, before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: “starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise,” each player “with at least one troop in the Conflict” may play any number or pass; “You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier.” Resolve after all players involved pass consecutively. Win-trigger cards are played “only after you've won, before moving to the next phase.”

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each gets the second reward. C and D still compete for the third reward; since C beats D, C gets it. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, including in two- and three-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops return to their supply, not their garrison.
answers.evidence: Tied for first: “no one wins the Conflict; each tied player receives the second reward,” and “the other two still compete for the third reward.” Tied for second: each gets third reward even in 2–3 player games; tied for third: nothing. “A player with 0 strength receives no reward.” Troops go to “their supply (not their garrison).”

answers.answer: Normal harvesting occurs when an Agent is sent to a Maker space and its space effect is resolved: Imperial Basin yields 1 base spice plus bonus spice, Hagga Basin 2 plus bonus, and The Great Flat 3 plus bonus. In Phase 4: Makers, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin; for each with no Agent, add 1 spice from the bank to any bonus spice already there. If an Agent moved away before Phase 4 and the space is empty then, bonus spice still accumulates there.
answers.evidence: Board spaces list the harvesting effects for Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, and The Great Flat. Phase 4 checks those three spaces and, if a space “has no Agent on it,” places 1 spice “as bonus spice, adding to any bonus spice already accumulated.” Maker-space clarification: if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately: the trigger is checked at the end of the round in Phase 5: Recall. The game also ends at that check if the Conflict Deck is empty, including when the last Conflict has been revealed earlier in the round. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then the player with the most VP wins. Tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Phase 5: Recall checks whether anyone is at 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Scoring says the trigger occurs “at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall)” and Endgame Intrigue cards resolve first. Tiebreaks: “spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops ... then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.”

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, you gain 1 VP; dropping below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4 Influence, you earn the track bonus, keep it if you later drop below 4, and can earn it again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 with a Faction takes its Alliance token and its VP. A holder tied at the same Influence is not overtaken; an opponent must rise to a higher space. If the holder loses Influence while tied with another player, the previously tied player takes the token; if several were tied, the holder chooses one.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: at 2, gain a VP “(lost if you drop below 2, regained if you reach 2 again)”; at 4, bonus is not given back and may be earned again. Alliances: first to 4 takes token and VP; opponent must rise to a “higher space”; “Merely tying the holder does not take it.” If holder loses Influence while previously tied, the tied player takes it; if several tied, holder chooses one.

answers.answer: Because the two opponents were tied with the Alliance holder, when the holder loses 1 Influence the holder chooses which of those previously tied opponents takes the Alliance. If instead the holder was the only player at 4 and falls to 3, they lose the token; if no player remains at 4 or higher, return it to the board. If another player is at 4 or higher, that player takes it.
answers.evidence: If an Alliance holder loses Influence while previously tied, the previously tied player takes it; “if several were tied, the holder chooses one.” The holder also loses it if falling to 3 or less; “if no player has 4 or more to take it, return it to the board.”

answers.answer: Discarding means moving a card from your hand, unless otherwise specified, to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash itself; a non-arrow instruction to trash itself is mandatory. You cannot reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffle only when unable to draw (and the summary specifically says Paul Atreides' ability or Poison Snooper cannot look at the top of an empty deck).
answers.evidence: “Discard” means a card from your hand ... to your discard pile. Trashing removes cards “from your hand, your discard pile, or in play” to the box; Reserve cards return to the Reserve stack. Trashing “is optional unless it's paying a cost or a card directs you to trash itself”; non-arrow self-trash is mandatory. Deck exhaustion: reshuffle when unable to draw; “You can't reshuffle early” to look at the top of an empty deck.

answers.answer: A player who wins a Conflict rewarding control of Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin places a Control marker on that space's flag, replacing any opponent's marker. The controller receives a bonus whenever any player, including the controller, sends an Agent there: 1 Solari for Arrakeen or Carthag, 1 spice for Imperial Basin. If a Conflict card is later revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict as a defensive bonus.
answers.evidence: Control: winning a matching Conflict places a marker “replacing any opponent's marker.” The controller receives the bonus whenever “any player, including yourself,” visits: 1 Solari for Arrakeen/Carthag or 1 spice for Imperial Basin. When a Conflict card is revealed for a controlled space, “you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.”

answers.answer: In two-player setup, choose an unused color, put one Rival cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks, put the remaining cubes in its supply, and leave its garrison without troops. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P; shuffle the remaining House Hagal cards and place its deck and three Agents near the supply. There is no Rival Leader or solo difficulty setup. After each First Player's Agent turn, House Hagal takes one Agent turn if it has an Agent in supply; it does not act after the other human's turn or after a Reveal turn. It has three Agents, never Reveals, does not collect resources, earn Conflict rewards or score VP, and can take/hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: House Hagal setup specifies unused color, cubes on four Influence tracks, no troops in garrison, removal of three 1P Arrakeen cards, remaining deck, and “three Agents.” It acts “after each of the First Player's Agent turns,” not after the other human or a Reveal. It “never takes a Reveal turn,” does not collect resources, earn Conflict rewards or score VP, but “can take and hold Faction Alliances.”

answers.answer: If a revealed card's indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. For a two-space card, use only the option matching current conditions; if that option is occupied, draw a new card and do not switch to the other option. Reshuffle Hagal cards immediately if its deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, then continue revealing. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the card's icons and instructions. Each troop icon recruits one troop: deploy it if this is a Combat space, otherwise put it in the Rival's garrison. Whenever it sends an Agent to a Combat space, it also deploys up to two garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Harvest Spice follows its card instructions; remove harvested bonus spice from the space and return it to the bank rather than accumulating it as a resource.
answers.evidence: Agent turns: if the indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until eligible. For two-space cards, if the condition-matching option is occupied, “draw a new card, never switch to the other option.” Reshuffle if deck empty or Reshuffle appears. Ignore space costs, requirements and effects. Troop icons recruit; Combat space troops deploy, otherwise garrison; on any Combat space also deploy up to two garrison troops. Harvest Spice removes bonus spice from the space and returns it to the bank.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if House Hagal has a troop in the Conflict, reveal a House Hagal card in turn order (reshuffling and revealing again if it is Reshuffle); count only its swords, adding 1 strength per sword to its normal 2 strength per deployed troop. Humans may then play Combat Intrigue before Combat resolves. House Hagal receives no reward but occupies its rank when human rewards are awarded. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and do not replace it. A tie for second gives each tied human the third reward even in a two-player game, although ordinary third place is unavailable.
answers.evidence: Combat: if Hagal has a troop, reveal a card; if Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again; “Ignore everything except the sword icons” and add them to “2 strength per deployed troop.” Humans may then play Combat Intrigue. Hagal gets no reward but “still occupies that rank.” If it wins a space a human controls, remove the marker and Hagal does not replace it. Summary's general tie rule gives third reward for a tie for second “including in two- and three-player games”; ordinary third place is 4-player only.
